item.title: Thoracic Central PA Mobilization
clinicalUse: Adjunct in selected neck/shoulder presentations when thoracic mobility is relevant
patientPosition: Prone with head supported and arms relaxed.
A pillow under the chest may be used if extension is uncomfortable.
therapistPosition: Stack shoulders over hands to use body weight rather than arm strength.
stabilization: The rib cage and table provide support.
Avoid allowing the trunk to roll during unilateral work.
contact: Place hypothenar eminence or supported thumbs over the target spinous process for central PA.
For unilateral PA, contact the transverse process/articular region as trained.
forceDirection: Posterior-to-anterior, approximately perpendicular to the local thoracic contour.
Use low grade for pain, higher grade for stiffness when safe.
steps: 1. Record thoracic extension/rotation or the functional task.
6. Follow with active thoracic extension/rotation or loaded upper-quarter work.
reassess: Neck/shoulder comparable sign if that was the reason for treatment
mistakes: Using thoracic mobilization when the thoracic spine is not clinically relevant.
safety: Use caution with osteoporosis, rib fracture history, inflammatory disease and recent trauma.
item.visualCue: Contact over thoracic segment → PA oscillation → Re-test thoracic or linked neck/shoulder movement.

subTechniques.name: Thoracic Central PA Mobilization
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve thoracic extension tolerance and local stiffness when clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Prone with head supported and breathing unrestricted.
subTechniques.contact: Hypothenar or supported-thumb contact over the spinous process; stack shoulders over hands to avoid excessive arm effort.
subTechniques.direction: Apply a posterior-to-anterior oscillation approximately perpendicular to the local thoracic contour.
subTechniques.reassess: Thoracic extension/rotation and any linked neck/shoulder comparable sign.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Use the lowest force that changes the comparable sign; more spring does not equal better treatment.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Use caution with osteoporosis, rib fracture history and recent trauma.

subTechniques.name: Thoracic Unilateral PA Mobilization
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Address side-specific thoracic stiffness when a unilateral PA improves rotation or a linked upper-quarter sign.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Prone with chest and head supported.
subTechniques.contact: Broad contact over the selected transverse-process/articular region while the trunk remains stable.
subTechniques.direction: Apply a unilateral posterior-to-anterior oscillation on the selected side.
subTechniques.reassess: Thoracic rotation and linked neck/shoulder movement.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Prevent trunk rolling; if the body rotates under your hand, the local glide is lost.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid painful direct loading over suspected rib injury.
